subject: Business Models
title: Business Model vs Product Innovation
description: A quick, practical guide to Business Model vs Product Innovation.

hook.text: Nespresso didn't invent coffee. It put coffee in capsules and sold machines cheaply. The model was the invention.

buildup.text: Product innovation improves what you sell. Business model innovation changes how you sell, deliver, or earn.

discovery.text: Nespresso's razor-blade model: cheap machines, expensive capsules. The coffee costs 5x more per cup than regular.

twist.text: Competitors matched the coffee quality easily. But replicating the capsule lock-in ecosystem took years.

climax.text: Business model innovation is harder to copy than product innovation. The model becomes the competitive moat.

punchline.text: Same coffee, 5x the price. The capsule model, not the beans, was the innovation.

quiz.question: What type of innovation did Nespresso primarily use?

details.summary: Product innovation improves what a company sells while business model innovation changes how a company creates and captures value. Many industry disruptions come not from better products but from fundamentally reimagining the revenue, distribution, or cost structure around them.
details.whyItMatters: Companies that focus only on product improvements miss disruptions driven by model changes. Uber did not invent better cars and Airbnb did not build better hotels; they reinvented the business models around existing assets.
takeaways: Product innovation improves features; model innovation changes the value logic
Disruptors often win by changing the model, not building a better product
Incumbents tend to over-invest in products and under-invest in model change

faq.question: Can you give an example of business model innovation beating product innovation?
faq.answer: Netflix did not make better DVDs. It changed the rental model from per-disc late fees to a flat monthly subscription, then shifted again to streaming. Blockbuster had a superior physical product network but lost because its model could not adapt.

faq.question: Why do incumbents struggle with business model innovation?
faq.answer: Existing revenue streams create internal resistance. Cannibalizing a profitable model feels risky even when disruption looms. Organizational structures and incentives are optimized for the current model, making fundamental change politically and operationally difficult.
